prompt:
Build a comprehensive, modern, mobile-first landing page builder heavily inspired by Swipe Pages. The primary objective is to create a platform that enables users to rapidly design, customize, and publish high-converting, mobile-optimized landing pages. The core defining feature must be the 'Mobile Slide' functionality—an interactive, swipeable format that perfectly mimics a native mobile app experience, tailored for social media traffic (e.g., TikTok, Instagram).

Your technical stack should be Next.js 15, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and SQLite for data persistence. Focus on delivering the following core functionalities:

1. Mobile-First Swipeable Builder: Implement a unique editor mode that specifically builds slide-based mobile experiences. Users should be able to create vertical or horizontal swipeable sections, just like Instagram stories or TikTok feeds. Include smooth micro-animations and gesture-based navigation support for the published output.
2. High-Performance Architecture: Structure the output generation to be incredibly fast, simulating AMP (Accelerated Mobile Pages) benefits. The published pages must pre-render content and achieve near-instantaneous load times to reduce bounce rates and improve conversions.
3. Intuitive Drag-and-Drop Interface: Build a robust, grid-based, no-code visual editor. It must include a sidebar with essential conversion-focused blocks: countdown timers, lead capture forms (with basic validation), pricing tables, and interactive CTA buttons. Allow users to easily snap these blocks into the mobile layout.
4. Data Persistence & Export: Store all user data, page configurations, and leads locally using SQLite. Ensure users can export their generated pages as highly optimized static HTML/CSS/JS bundles so they aren't locked into the platform.
5. Realistic Workflow: Provide a complete end-to-end loop: starting from a blank slide, adding elements, configuring styling (colors, typography), previewing the exact mobile experience, and hitting 'publish' to generate the static files.

Make the default mode single-user and private. Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts. Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example. Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end. Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states. Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents. Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow. Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works. Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
